chunks: ‘Isa ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman narrated to us from his father, who said:

Ibn ‘Ukasha ibn Mihsan al-Asadi entered upon Abu Ja‘far, and Abu ‘Abd Allah (عليه السلام) was standing with him. He presented grapes to him, and he said: “One by one is how the very old man and the very young child eat; three and four at a time is how one who thinks he will not be satisfied eats; and eat it two by two, for that is recommended.”

Then he said to Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام): “Why do you not marry Abu ‘Abd Allah, for he has reached the age of marriage?” He said: There was before him a sealed purse, and he said: “Indeed, a slave trader from the people of Barbar will soon come and lodge at the house of Maymun, and we shall buy for him a slave-girl with this purse.”

He said: Then what was to occur occurred. One day we entered upon Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام), and he said: “Shall I inform you about the slave trader whom I mentioned to you? He has arrived, so go and buy a slave-girl from him with this purse.” He said: So we went to the slave trader, and he said: “I have sold all that I had except for two sick slave-girls, one of whom is better than the other.” We said: “Bring them out so that we may look at them.” So he brought them out, and we said: “For how much will you sell us this one of sounder condition?” He said: “For seventy dinars.” We said: “Be fair.”

He said: “I will not reduce it from seventy dinars.” We said to him: “We will buy her from you with this purse, whatever amount it reaches, and we do not know what is in it.” There was with him a man white of head and beard, who said: “Open it and weigh it.” The slave trader said: “Do not open it, for if it is deficient by even one grain from seventy dinars, I will not transact with you.” Then the old man said: “Come near.” So we came near, broke the seal, and weighed the dinars, and it was exactly seventy dinars, neither more nor less.

So we took the slave-girl and brought her to Abu Ja‘far (عليه السلام), while Ja‘far was standing with him. We informed Abu Ja‘far of what had happened, so he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said to her: “What is your name?” She said: “Hamidah.” He said: “Hamidah in this world, praiseworthy in the Hereafter.” Then he said: “O Ja‘far, take her to yourself,” and she gave birth to the best of the people of the earth, Musa ibn Ja‘far (عليه السلام).

key_terms.حَمِيدَةُ: the name of the woman purchased for Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام)
key_terms.صُرَّةٌ مَخْتُومَةٌ: a sealed purse prepared for the purchase
key_terms.عِنَبًا: grapes, mentioned in the etiquette of eating
key_terms.مُوسَىٰ بْنَ جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Musa ibn Ja‘far (عليه السلام), whose birth is mentioned at the end
key_terms.يُسْتَحَبُّ: recommended; indicating a preferred manner of doing something

ai.seo_question: How does al-Kafi describe the marriage of Imam Ja‘far al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) to Hamidah and the birth of Imam Musa al-Kazim (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This narration recounts the foretold arrival and purchase of Hamidah for Imam Ja‘far al-Sadiq (عليه السلام), culminating in the birth of Imam Musa ibn Ja‘far (عليه السلام). It also preserves a brief teaching on eating grapes with propriety and presents a biographical account connected to the noble lineage of the Ahl al-Bayt (عليهم السلام).
